bull_bear.body:
- Vertically integrated operations across both cotton and polyester value chains, from spinning/polymerization to finished garments and home textiles.
- Diversified product, customer, and market mix spanning domestic, export, and converter-country channels, providing risk mitigation.
- Strong promoter background and group synergies with Reliance Industries Limited, supporting sustainability in challenging environments.
- Standalone credit rating of CARE AA+, reflecting strong business fundamentals.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility and availability (cotton) — Cotton is the primary raw material; as an agricultural commodity, its prices are affected by weather, government policies, duties, and global supply-demand. This directly impacts cost of production and profitability.
- Export market concentration and tariff exposure (USA) — The USA reciprocal tariff regime escalated to 50% on Indian textile exports from August 2025, materially impacting export realizations. Policy uncertainty around the Bilateral Trade Agreement and relative tariff positioning versus competitors like Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Vietnam can rapidly redirect buyer sourcing decisions.
- Demand slowdown and fashion trend shifts in value-added segments — Performance depends on demand in individual business segments. Apparel Fabrics and Home Textiles are subject to fashion trends and consumer demand. Major international conflicts also impact demand from impacted economies and global markets.
- Shipping route disruptions and elevated freight costs — Ongoing disruptions to Red Sea shipping routes due to the Houthi conflict have continued to affect freight costs and transit times on key India-to-USA and India-to-Europe trade lanes, impacting export margin realizations and on-time delivery reliability.
- Financial risk from high debt and interest rate sensitivity — Outstanding term loans of â¹3,456.26 crores and working capital limits of â¹300 crores expose the company to interest obligations and repayment requirements. Loans are linked to MCLR, so any increase would raise interest costs.
- Currency exposure risk — Significant export volumes expose the company to currency fluctuations. While a natural hedge exists due to lower imports, adverse movements can impact export realizations and profitability.
- Government policy and regulatory changes — Business is impacted by changes in export/import policies, customs duty structures, export incentives, and GST rates, which can alter competitive dynamics and cost structures.
- Information technology and cybersecurity risk — IT is the backbone of operations. Legacy system migration, cybersecurity threats, and the need for continuous security architecture enhancements pose operational and data integrity risks.

business.body: Alok Industries operates a fully integrated textile manufacturing setup spanning spinning, weaving, processing, finished fabrics, home textiles, and garments in cotton, and continuous polymerization through to polyester yarns and staple fiber in polyester. The company serves a diversified customer base including global retail brands, textile importers, private labels, domestic retailers, garment exporters, and manufacturers across the world. Its operations are supported by large-scale, flexible plants in Vapi and Silvassa.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Spinning:** Cotton and blended yarns in various counts
- **Polyester:** Polyester Chips, Partially Oriented Yarn (POY), Fully Drawn Yarn (FDY), Drawn Texturized Yarn (DTY), Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF)
- **Home Textiles:** Bedsheets, Towels
- **Apparel & Fabric:** Finished fabrics, Garments

outlook.body:
- Shift major polyester business to Manufacturing Capacity Booking (Job-work model) from March 2024.
- Elevate sustainability from compliance to core strategic priority, driving transformation across the value chain centred on circularity, renewable energy, and resource efficiency.
- Accelerate transition toward high-performance, sustainable fiber by leveraging Reliance Industries Limited's advanced Recron technologies (Kooltex, Green Gold) for a strategic shift toward technical home textiles and specialized blends.
- No explicit dividend policy, buyback, or reinvestment philosophy stated. The Board's Report confirms no buyback, no issue of shares with differential rights, no ESOP, and no change in capital structure during the year. CSR obligation is nil due to negative average net profit over the preceding three years.
- CSR Policy adopted in line with Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013; however, no CSR spend was required during the year as the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years was negative.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Alok Industries operates vertically integrated facilities across cotton and polyester value chains. In cotton, integration spans spinning, weaving, processing, finished fabrics, bedsheets, towels, and garments. In polyester, integration runs from continuous polymerization to chips, POY, FDY, DTY, and PSF. The company has shifted its major polyester business to a Manufacturing Capacity Booking (Job-work model) from March 2024. Spinning facilities are located in Silvassa, with weaving and major stitching for bedding also at Silvassa, fabric processing at Vapi, and the entire terry-towel manufacturing at Vapi. The report does not disclose any new capacity addition, commissioning timelines, or specific expansion projects for the reporting period or future.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global apparel brands accelerating supply chain diversification away from Bangladesh, a structural shift favoring large, integrated Indian manufacturers.
- Bangladesh graduating from LDC status on November 24, 2026, making India more competitive, reinforced by FTAs with UK and EU.
- Domestic apparel market projected to grow at ~9% CAGR to US$ 180 billion by 2030, driven by rising incomes, urbanization, GST rationalization, and evolving consumer preferences.
- Recovery in embroidery demand expected gradually as inflationary pressures ease in US/EU and consumer discretionary spending stabilises.
- Growth in home textiles driven by India's new FTAs with EU and UK, increasing demand for sustainable/certified products, and supply chain diversification by global brands.
- India's competitive strength in cotton-based woven fabrics supported by rising preference for natural fibers and shifting sourcing strategy.
- Increase demand in active wear and government PLI scheme on synthetic segment expected to strengthen India's global position.

deepdive.thesis: Alok Industries is one of India's largest vertically integrated textile companies with unique integration across both Cotton and Polyester segments, serving global retail brands, importers, and domestic manufacturers.

open.item: Continue to target a diverse mix of international market, garment export trade, and domestic market to mitigate risk.

Ongoing geopolitical disturbances, including Middle East conflicts and Russia-Ukraine situation, continue to disrupt key export markets, elevate input and logistics costs, and weaken consumer sentiment.
Rising protectionist measures and trade restrictions across major economies are impacting export opportunities.

GST 2.0 reforms effective September 2025 raised concessional 5% GST threshold on readymade garments to ₹2,500 per piece and reduced GST on man-made fiber to 5% and man-made yarns to 5%, expected to stimulate domestic consumption and improve MMF manufacturing competitiveness.
India-EU FTA concluded in January 2026, once ratified and in force, will eliminate tariffs on a significant portion of T&A exports, potentially strengthening India's competitive positioning.

Alok Industries has elevated sustainability from a compliance requirement to a core strategic priority, driving a comprehensive transformation across its value chain centred on circularity, renewable energy, and resource efficiency.

Alok accelerated its transition toward high-performance, sustainable fiber by leveraging Reliance Industries Limited's advanced Recron technologies, including Kooltex and Green Gold, enabling a strategic shift in its product portfolio toward technical home textiles and specialized blends.
